title: A free answer allows wanted reassurance

captions.physics: Returning to an invitation heard differently
captions.energy: Beginning a remark without compulsory preparation
captions.emotions: Feeling attached to a wanted confirmation

meaning: You can return to an invitation to speak heard differently and begin without compulsory preparation, noticing attachment to wanted confirmation without making it conversation’s price.
text: Judgement in the physical position of your Vishuddha appears in returning to an invitation to speak now heard differently. The Fool in energy supports readiness to begin a remark without compulsory preparation. The Devil in emotions brings attachment to a wanted confirmation. You can understand that a question allows a living reply while still wanting a phrase known beforehand. Strong desire does not prescribe another person’s words.

For example, you return to “Do not prepare, just say it”. Previously heard as demanding a quick correct answer, it now becomes an invitation to your own thought. **A free beginning guarantees no wanted confirmation**. You can reply unexpectedly and honestly. Yet “You understood everything correctly” may feel necessary, as though the entire exchange otherwise failed. This pull can be named without declaring other words empty; genuine participation remains possible beside clarification, doubt or a different assessment of what was heard.

Difficulty arises if each fresh remark is judged only by whether wanted reassurance comes closer. A hidden script guides the free answer again. The constructive Fool helps leave the course open, including words unexpected. You can want confirmation and hear an actual thought; attachment need not disappear immediately, but an imperfect match to a formula proves neither absent attention nor a broken promise always to support an identical conclusion.
